### LOW: Opt\-in resident RAM prefix\-checkpoint bank contradicts T\-041's 'no production RAM tier' posture
[changelog\.d/nemotron\-super\-media\-discovery\.md:57](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/f8a2f79115a73bdd5a5c20bd5c4636f78a74f780/changelog.d/nemotron-super-media-discovery.md#L57) · A-001, T-028, T-041

The changelog adds \`DARKBLOOM\_PREFIX\_CACHE\_MEMORY=1\`, which opts the Nemotron Super owner into exact text prefix reuse through a resident recurrent checkpoint bank\. The bank is sized at min\(1 GiB, grant/8\) and reserved from load until retirement\. T\-041 and its mitigations say production never constructs or funds a resident\-RAM prefix cache and that there is no production RAM tier\. docs/architecture/hardware\-support\.md still says \`ramPrefix\` is always 0\. This is a new cross\-request reuse surface: a hit skips prefill, so first\-token latency leaks whether another prompt shared the prefix \(the T\-041 TTFT oracle\)\. Retained checkpoints also leave decoded prompt\-derived state resident in process memory after the request completes \(T\-028\)\. The visible text does not say whether the bank is keyed by the coordinator\-authored cacheSalt or whether it is bound to model build and prompt contract\. It does say client prompt\-cache keys are rejected, but that does not establish tenant isolation\. The T\-041 sign\-off, the DARKBLOOM\_PREFIX\_CACHE kill\-switch semantics and the TTL bounds do not obviously cover this path\. Fix: update T\-041 and TB\-007 to describe this tier; state its scope key, eviction and TTL bounds, and whether the DARKBLOOM\_PREFIX\_CACHE=0 kill switch also disables it; and require salt\-scoped lookup before the owner is registered or enabled for multi\-tenant traffic\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Threat model lacks coverage for the new resident\-RAM, unscoped prefix cache in the Nemotron Super local owner
[docs/architecture/inference\.md:142](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/f8a2f79115a73bdd5a5c20bd5c4636f78a74f780/docs/architecture/inference.md#L142) · A-001, T-041

The new doc text describes an opt\-in resident recurrent checkpoint bank \(DARKBLOOM\_PREFIX\_CACHE\_MEMORY=1\) in which text requests are submitted with prefix caching on and a 'local unscoped cache scope'\. T\-041 states that production has no resident\-RAM prefix cache or tier composition\. It also states that cache scope is coordinator\-authored from account, model build and prompt contract\. The new owner has no per\-account scope and uses a different env gate from the DARKBLOOM\_PREFIX\_CACHE kill switch\. If the loopback HTTP hook \(NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP\) or a later production caller serves multiple clients, they share one cache\. A client could then use a TTFT hit/miss timing oracle against another client's prefixes\. The doc says no production caller installs the hook, so this is not an active regression\. T\-041 should record the new tier and its scope assumptions before any registration or route is added\. The review could not check whether DARKBLOOM\_PREFIX\_CACHE=0 also disables this bank\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

findings.detail: The changelog adds `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1`, which opts the Nemotron Super owner into exact text prefix reuse. It uses a resident recurrent checkpoint bank sized at min(1 GiB, grant/8) and reserved from load until retirement. T-041 and hardware-support.md state that production never constructs a resident-RAM prefix cache, that ramPrefix is always 0, and that SSD is the sole tier. The changelog does not say that cross-account scoping (coordinator-authored cacheSalt) or the SEC-035 TTFT-oracle sign-off applies to this bank. It does say client prompt-cache keys are rejected, which leaves it unclear what scopes reuse. If the hook is served to multiple tenants, one account can detect another's prefix by hit/miss latency. The current text also gives no TTL or purge for the bank. The code is not in this batch, so this is a threat-model gap rather than a confirmed bug. Fix: add the RAM tier and its scoping, TTL and kill-switch semantics to T-041, or state that the hook is single-tenant/local only. Make the bank require an authenticated per-account salt before it can be enabled for coordinator traffic.
